Retry-After.description: How many seconds to wait before retrying.

X-Correlation-Id.description: The correlation identifier of this request. It is accepted on the request and echoed on every response, and it is the identifier a support call names.

BadRequest.description: The request was not valid. The body is problem details with per-field `errors` when the failure is a validation failure.

Forbidden.description: The caller holds a session but not the permission, the branch reach or the session assurance this operation requires. The refusal is audited.

InternalServerError.description: The request failed unexpectedly. The body carries the problem type and the correlation identifier and nothing else — never a stack trace, never an exception message.

NotFound.description: There is no such resource, or none this caller may see. The two are deliberately indistinguishable, so that the identifier space cannot be probed.

TooManyRequests.description: The rate-limit policy this operation declares refused the request. `Retry-After` says when it is worth trying again.

Unauthorized.description: There is no live session, or the one presented has expired or been revoked. The client re-authenticates in place and retries the request with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

UpgradeRequired.description: The client build declared in `X-Client-Version` is older than the minimum this server supports. Reloading collects the current build; repeating the request does not help. The body carries `minimumClient` and `current`.

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 9457 problem details. Every failure is reported in this shape, and never as a stack trace, an exception message or a bare status code.

code.description: The stable error code, `<module>.<kebab-case-reason>` — for example `idempotency.key-reused`. This is what a client branches on.

correlationId.description: The correlation identifier of the request, echoed so a support call can name it.

currentEtag.description: The same token in `ETag` form, ready to be sent back as `If-Match`.

currentVersion.description: The aggregate's current concurrency token, on a version conflict, so the client can re-read and merge without a second round trip.

detail.description: What went wrong on this occurrence, in words a person can act on.

errors.description: Field errors, keyed by the field's name in the request payload. Present on validation failures only.

instance.description: The request path this occurrence refers to.

retryable.description: True when repeating the identical request may succeed. A retry of a command reuses the same `Idempotency-Key`.

status.description: The HTTP status code, repeated so the body is self-contained.

title.description: A short, human-readable summary of the problem type.

type.description: The problem type, as `urn:tailor360:problem:<code>`. Stable across releases; a client may branch on it.

ProblemDetails.title: Problem details

antiForgeryToken.description: The request half of the anti-forgery token pair, fetched from `GET /api/v1/antiforgery` and held in memory. Required on every state-changing request, including signing in: a sign-in forged from another origin would plant the attacker's account in the victim's browser. It is useless without the paired cookie, which script cannot read.
antiForgeryToken.name: X-CSRF-Token

sessionCookie.description: An opaque server-side session identifier. The browser sends it automatically; script cannot read it, and no operation ever returns it. It is issued by signing in and is rotated on every change of assurance.
sessionCookie.name: __Host-t360.session

info.description:
The staff surface is `/api/v1/**`, served from the same origin as the client so that the
session travels in a cookie script cannot read. The major version lives in the URL and
nothing else negotiates it; inside a major version only additive changes are permitted, and
a breaking one is refused by the diff gate unless it is approved and its deprecation is
recorded (`docs/architecture/conventions.md` section 5).

Every request and response carries `X-Correlation-Id`. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details
with a stable `code` and, for validation failures, per-field `errors`; no error ever carries
a stack trace or an exception message. Commands that a client may retry take an
`Idempotency-Key`; editable aggregates carry an `ETag` and require `If-Match`.

This document is generated from the composed route table and committed to
`docs/api/openapi.v1.json`. It is not written by hand, and an endpoint that does not appear
in it fails the endpoint inventory test.
